name: applications-unavailable
description:
The per-computer applications call fails, and the run must finish anyway. This is a regression test for an unbounded loop in get_apps(): its `if err:` branch printed the failure and fell through to the next iteration of `while True:`, re-issuing the identical request forever, and a 2xx with an empty body (which get_json decodes to None) matched neither `if err:` nor `elif data:` and spun the same way. Neither path could ever reach the `break`, so a single computer whose applications endpoint was unhappy hung the whole task -- no assets imported, not even the computers already fetched. The sibling get_computers() always had the `break`; get_apps() is now the same shape.

Both spinning paths are covered here, one per computer, because they are separate branches and the fix has to close both:

  9101 -> 403 with a body, the `if err:` path. 403 is deliberate: get_json retries 408/425/429/500/502/503/504 by default, so a 500 would be answered four times per iteration with exponential backoff and the loop would present as a hung task rather than a fast spin. A status outside that list makes each iteration cheap, which is what turns an infinite loop into an assertion the harness can actually make -- see `request_count` below.
  9102 -> 200 with a zero-length body, the falsy-data path. get_json returns (None, None) for it, so this is the case where nothing was wrong and nothing was returned.
  9103 -> a normal application row, so the scenario also proves the fix did not turn the working path into an early exit.

`request_count: 4` is the assertion that actually pins termination: one computers call plus exactly ONE applications call per computer. Before the fix this run did not merely emit fewer assets, it never returned -- the harness failed with a subprocess timeout after issuing hundreds of thousands of requests. asset_count and the per-asset fields then pin the intended degradation: all three computers still import, with their identity, addressing and device type intact, and the two whose applications could not be read simply carry no software.

check_determinism is left on: a re-run answers identically, so both the ids and the partial software set are stable rather than dependent on which call happened to fail.

namespaced_ids is skipped for the same reason as the happy scenario: the asset id is the bare SLM computer Id with no customer scope, so two Snow customers imported into one runZero account would collide. Pre-existing, not introduced here.

json.Message: The user does not have access to application data.

log_contains: failed to retrieve application for 9101 at $skip=0: status 403
